-- =============================================================================
-- 0002_tenancy.sql — users, organizations (tenants), settings, memberships/roles
-- =============================================================================
-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
--
-- Model: a USER is a global identity (one login, many organizations). An
-- ORGANIZATION is the tenant boundary — "organization" and "workspace" are the
-- same concept in this product. ORGANIZATION_MEMBERS is the many-to-many link that
-- also carries the user's ROLE in that organization (RBAC is per organization).
--
-- Why many-to-many (a membership table) instead of `users.organization_id`:
--   If every user belonged to exactly one organization — typical of a product sold
--   to single companies — organization_id and role could simply be columns on
--   `users` (one organization → many users), and organization_members would not
--   exist. That assumption does not hold for a project-management platform.
--   Example: a group that runs several companies — Compliance Foundry, Comperis
--   Cybersecurity and Fixpliance AI — is three organizations, each with its own
--   projects, members and settings, yet the same people may work in two or all
--   three of them. They should use ONE login and switch between organizations,
--   not hold three accounts. So one organization has many users AND one user has
--   many organizations: many-to-many, which needs a link table.
--   The link row is also the only correct home for the ROLE: the same person can
--   be an admin in one organization and a viewer in another, which a single
--   users.role column cannot express.
--   Cost: "what may this user do here?" is a membership lookup rather than a
--   column read — one index-only scan (organization_members_user_idx below).
-- =============================================================================


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Roles, in ascending order of power.
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- A Postgres enum (not text + CHECK) because enum values compare by declaration
-- order: `role >= 'admin'` means "admin or owner", which is how every permission
-- check in 0005 is written. Adding a role later is `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE …
-- BEFORE/AFTER`, which preserves the ordering.
--   viewer — read-only access to everything in the organization
--   member — creates and edits tasks, comments, labels
--   admin  — manages projects, statuses, settings and non-owner members
--   owner  — everything, incl. managing owners and deleting the organization
CREATE TYPE organization_role AS ENUM ('viewer', 'member', 'admin', 'owner');


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- users — global identities
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Authentication is out of scope (no password/IdP columns); in production this row
-- would be keyed to an identity provider subject.
CREATE TABLE users (
  id            uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  email         text        NOT NULL,
  display_name  text        NOT NULL,
  avatar_url    text,
  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT users_email_unique UNIQUE (email),
  -- Stored normalised (trimmed + lower-case), so the plain UNIQUE above is
  -- effectively case-insensitive without the citext extension.
  CONSTRAINT users_email_normalized CHECK (email = lower(btrim(email)) AND email LIKE '%_@_%'),
  CONSTRAINT users_display_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(display_name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  CONSTRAINT users_avatar_url_length CHECK (avatar_url IS NULL OR char_length(avatar_url) <= 2048)
);

CREATE TRIGGER users_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON users
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- organizations — the tenant
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE organizations (
  id          uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  name        text        NOT NULL,
  -- URL identifier: app.example.com/acme/… Lower-case, digits, inner hyphens.
  slug        text        NOT NULL,
  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT organizations_slug_unique UNIQUE (slug),
  CONSTRAINT organizations_slug_format CHECK (slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,46}[a-z0-9])?$'),
  CONSTRAINT organizations_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100)
);

CREATE TRIGGER organizations_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON organizations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- organization_settings — organization-level (workspace-level) settings
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- One row per organization, with TYPED columns rather than a jsonb bag: each
-- setting gets a real type, a default and a CHECK, and adding a setting is a
-- reviewed migration. (jsonb is the right call only for user-defined/unknown keys.)
-- Kept apart from `organizations` because settings are edited by a different
-- audience (admins) and change on a different cadence than the tenant identity.
CREATE TABLE organization_settings (
  organization_id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- IANA zone that defines "today" for the organization — and therefore what
  -- "overdue" means (a task due on the 20th is overdue from the 21st *there*).
  timezone                     text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
  -- First day of the week in calendar views: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday (ISO: 1).
  week_starts_on               smallint    NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
  -- Lets admins decide whether plain members may create projects; enforced by
  -- the projects INSERT policy in 0005 (settings drive authorization).
  members_can_create_projects  boolean     NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
  updated_at                   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  -- Evaluating a zone conversion rejects unknown zone names ("Mars/Olympus") with
  -- an error, so only real IANA zones are ever stored.
  CONSTRAINT organization_settings_timezone_valid CHECK ((now() AT TIME ZONE timezone) IS NOT NULL),
  CONSTRAINT organization_settings_week_starts_on_range CHECK (week_starts_on BETWEEN 0 AND 6)
);

CREATE TRIGGER organization_settings_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON organization_settings
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();

-- Every organization always has a settings row (created with the defaults), so
-- readers never need a LEFT JOIN + COALESCE. SECURITY DEFINER: the settings row
-- is created on behalf of whoever created the organization, whatever their grants.
CREATE FUNCTION app.organizations_create_settings() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO public.organization_settings (organization_id) VALUES (NEW.id);
  RETURN NULL; -- AFTER trigger: return value ignored
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER organizations_create_settings
  AFTER INSERT ON organizations
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.organizations_create_settings();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- organization_members — who belongs to which organization, with which role
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- The users ↔ organizations many-to-many link (rationale: header of this file).
CREATE TABLE organization_members (
  organization_id  uuid              NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Deleting a user removes their memberships (their tasks become unassigned via
  -- the ON DELETE SET NULL on tasks — see 0003).
  user_id          uuid              NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role             organization_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
  created_at       timestamptz       NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- "joined at"
  updated_at       timestamptz       NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  -- PK serves "who is in organization X" (organization_id first) and is the
  -- target of tasks' composite assignee FK.
  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id, user_id)
);

-- The reverse direction, "which organizations is user Y in, with what role", runs
-- at the start of EVERY request (row-level security). Covering index: the
-- membership lookup is answered from the index alone (index-only scan).
CREATE INDEX organization_members_user_idx
  ON organization_members (user_id, organization_id) INCLUDE (role);

CREATE TRIGGER organization_members_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON organization_members
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Invariant: an organization always has at least one owner
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Not expressible as a CHECK (it spans rows), so it is a CONSTRAINT TRIGGER.
-- DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED: the check runs at COMMIT, so ownership can be
-- transferred in one transaction (promote the new owner, then demote/remove the
-- old one) without tripping on the intermediate state.
-- Deleting the whole organization is allowed: by commit time the organization row
-- is gone, so there is nothing left to protect.
CREATE FUNCTION app.organization_keeps_an_owner() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF OLD.role = 'owner'
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.organizations o WHERE o.id = OLD.organization_id)
     AND NOT EXISTS (
       SELECT 1 FROM public.organization_members m
        WHERE m.organization_id = OLD.organization_id AND m.role = 'owner')
  THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'organization % must keep at least one owner', OLD.organization_id
      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation',
            HINT = 'Promote another member to owner before removing or demoting this one.';
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER organization_members_keep_an_owner
  AFTER UPDATE OF role OR DELETE ON organization_members
  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.organization_keeps_an_owner();

1	-- =============================================================================
2	-- 0003_projects_and_tasks.sql — projects, customizable statuses, labels, tasks
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
5	--
6	--   organization ─┬─< project ─┬─< task_status   (each project defines its columns)
7	--                 │            └─< task >── task_status, assignee (a member)
8	--                 └─< label >──< task_label >── task
9	-- =============================================================================
10	
11	
12	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
13	-- Enums
14	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
15	-- Ordered so that `ORDER BY priority DESC` lists urgent first and none last.
16	CREATE TYPE task_priority AS ENUM ('none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent');
17	
18	-- Statuses are custom per project ("QA", "Blocked", "Shipped"…), but the system
19	-- still needs to know what a status MEANS. Every custom status maps to one fixed
20	-- category; "open", "overdue", "completed" and cycle-time logic use the category,
21	-- never status names. (Same approach as Linear's workflow-state types.)
22	CREATE TYPE status_category AS ENUM ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started', 'completed', 'canceled');
23	
24	
25	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	-- projects
27	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	CREATE TABLE projects (
29	  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
30	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
31	  -- Short prefix for human task identifiers: key "WEB" + number 42 → "WEB-42".
32	  -- Not updatable by the API (0005), so identifiers never change once shared.
33	  key              text        NOT NULL,
34	  name             text        NOT NULL,
35	  description      text,
36	  -- Last task number handed out in this project; the next task gets +1 (see
37	  -- app.tasks_before_insert). It exists only to give tasks short, per-project,
38	  -- human-readable identifiers — WEB-1, WEB-2, … — used in the UI, URLs, commit
39	  -- messages and conversation ("is WEB-42 done?"). Alternatives rejected:
40	  --   * max(number) + 1 at insert time — two concurrent inserts read the same
41	  --     max and collide (unique violation), unless the project is locked anyway;
42	  --   * one SEQUENCE per project — thousands of schema objects created at
43	  --     runtime, outside migrations, awkward to copy/restore per tenant;
44	  --   * a global sequence — unique, but not per project (WEB-48213, and it leaks
45	  --     platform-wide volume).
46	  -- An atomic `UPDATE … RETURNING` on this column is O(1) and race-free. Cost:
47	  -- concurrent task inserts into the SAME project queue on this row's lock until
48	  -- the inserting transaction commits (different projects never contend).
49	  task_counter     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
50	  -- Projects are archived, never deleted by the API: their tasks are history.
51	  archived_at      timestamptz,
52	  created_by       uuid        DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
53	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
54	  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
55	
56	  -- Redundant with the PK on its own, but required as the TARGET of composite
57	  -- foreign keys (organization_id, project_id) from child tables — that is what
58	  -- guarantees a child row's organization_id equals its project's.
59	  CONSTRAINT projects_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
60	  -- Also serves "list an organization's projects" (organization_id is leading).
61	  CONSTRAINT projects_key_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, key),
62	  CONSTRAINT projects_key_format CHECK (key ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}$'),
63	  CONSTRAINT projects_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
64	  CONSTRAINT projects_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 10000),
65	  CONSTRAINT projects_task_counter_non_negative CHECK (task_counter >= 0)
66	);
67	
68	-- Column list: only user-visible edits bump updated_at, not the task counter that
69	-- every task insert increments.
70	CREATE TRIGGER projects_set_updated_at
71	  BEFORE UPDATE OF name, description, archived_at ON projects
72	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
73	
74	
75	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
76	-- task_statuses — the customizable board columns of ONE project
77	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	CREATE TABLE task_statuses (
79	  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
80	  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
81	  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
82	  name             text            NOT NULL,
83	  category         status_category NOT NULL,
84	  color            text            NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
85	  -- Column order on the board. A project has a handful of statuses, so reordering
86	  -- simply rewrites the positions in one transaction (no fractional keys needed).
87	  position         integer         NOT NULL,
88	  -- The status new tasks get when none is specified.
89	  is_default       boolean         NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
90	  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
91	  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
92	
93	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
94	    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
95	  -- Target of tasks' composite FK (project_id, status_id): a task can only use
96	  -- a status of its OWN project.
97	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_id_id_unique UNIQUE (project_id, id),
98	  -- New work must not start out "done": the default must be an open category.
99	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_default_is_open CHECK (NOT is_default OR category IN ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started')),
100	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
101	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
102	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_position_non_negative CHECK (position >= 0)
103	);
104	
105	-- Status names are unique per project, ignoring case ("Done" vs "done").
106	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_name_unique ON task_statuses (project_id, lower(name));
107	-- At most one default per project (a partial unique index: only rows WHERE
108	-- is_default participate). "At least one" is handled by the fallback in
109	-- app.tasks_before_insert.
110	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_one_default_per_project ON task_statuses (project_id) WHERE is_default;
111	
112	CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_set_updated_at
113	  BEFORE UPDATE ON task_statuses
114	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
115	
116	-- Every new project starts with a usable board. SECURITY DEFINER because members
117	-- may create projects (if the organization allows) but only admins may manage
118	-- statuses directly.
119	CREATE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses() RETURNS trigger
120	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
121	AS $$
122	BEGIN
123	  INSERT INTO public.task_statuses (organization_id, project_id, name, category, color, position, is_default)
124	  VALUES
125	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Backlog',     'backlog',   '#94a3b8', 0, false),
126	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Todo',        'unstarted', '#64748b', 1, true),
127	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'In Progress', 'started',   '#f59e0b', 2, false),
128	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Done',        'completed', '#22c55e', 3, false),
129	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Canceled',    'canceled',  '#ef4444', 4, false);
130	  RETURN NULL;
131	END
132	$$;
133	
134	CREATE TRIGGER projects_create_default_statuses
135	  AFTER INSERT ON projects
136	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses();
137	
138	
139	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
140	-- labels — organization-wide tags
141	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	-- Scoped to the organization, not the project, so one "bug" label can be used and
143	-- filtered across every project (cross-project reporting).
144	CREATE TABLE labels (
145	  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
146	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
147	  name             text        NOT NULL,
148	  color            text        NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
149	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
150	  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
151	
152	  CONSTRAINT labels_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
153	  CONSTRAINT labels_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
154	  CONSTRAINT labels_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50)
155	);
156	
157	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX labels_name_unique ON labels (organization_id, lower(name));
158	
159	CREATE TRIGGER labels_set_updated_at
160	  BEFORE UPDATE ON labels
161	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
162	
163	
164	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	-- tasks
166	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
167	CREATE TABLE tasks (
168	  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
169	  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
170	  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
171	  -- Per-project sequence number, assigned by trigger (never by the client).
172	  number           integer         NOT NULL,
173	  title            text            NOT NULL,
174	  description      text,           -- Markdown
175	  -- Optional on INSERT: the trigger fills in the project's default status.
176	  status_id        uuid            NOT NULL,
177	  -- DENORMALISED copy of task_statuses.category, maintained by triggers (below).
178	  -- Why: "open"/"overdue" are the hottest filters, and a partial index can only
179	  -- use columns of its own table — this keeps "my overdue tasks" a single index
180	  -- range scan instead of a join through task_statuses.
181	  status_category  status_category NOT NULL,
182	  priority         task_priority   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
183	  -- Single assignee (the Linear/Jira model): keeps "tasks per assignee"
184	  -- unambiguous and ownership clear. A task_assignees join table is the
185	  -- migration path if multi-assignee is ever needed.
186	  assignee_id      uuid,
187	  due_date         date,
188	  -- Card order within a board column, as a fractional index key ("a0", "a0V",
189	  -- "a1"…): a card dropped between two others gets a key between theirs, so a
190	  -- move rewrites ONE row instead of renumbering the column. Keys are generated by
191	  -- the API. COLLATE "C" = plain byte order, which those keys are designed for;
192	  -- a linguistic collation (en_US) would order them incorrectly.
193	  rank             text            COLLATE "C" NOT NULL,
194	  -- Set while the task is in a 'completed' status (trigger-maintained); feeds
195	  -- "completed this week" and cycle-time reporting.
196	  completed_at     timestamptz,
197	  created_by       uuid            DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
198	  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
199	  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
200	  -- Soft delete: deleted tasks keep their comments and history and can be
201	  -- restored. Hot indexes below exclude them.
202	  deleted_at       timestamptz,
203	
204	  -- Tenant consistency: the task's organization IS its project's organization.
205	  CONSTRAINT tasks_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
206	    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
207	  -- The status must belong to the task's project. Deleting a status that still
208	  -- has tasks is refused (move them first). Default NO ACTION, not RESTRICT, so a
209	  -- cascading project/organization delete can remove tasks and statuses together.
210	  CONSTRAINT tasks_status_fk FOREIGN KEY (project_id, status_id)
211	    REFERENCES task_statuses (project_id, id),
212	  -- The assignee must be a MEMBER of the task's organization. When the membership
213	  -- ends, only assignee_id is cleared (Postgres 15+ column-list SET NULL) —
214	  -- organization_id, part of the same key, is of course kept.
215	  CONSTRAINT tasks_assignee_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, assignee_id)
216	    REFERENCES organization_members (organization_id, user_id) ON DELETE SET NULL (assignee_id),
217	
218	  CONSTRAINT tasks_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id), -- composite FK target
219	  -- Also the index behind identifier lookups ("WEB-42" → project + number).
220	  CONSTRAINT tasks_number_unique UNIQUE (project_id, number),
221	  CONSTRAINT tasks_title_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
222	  CONSTRAINT tasks_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 50000),
223	  CONSTRAINT tasks_rank_not_empty CHECK (rank <> ''),
224	  -- The two trigger-maintained columns can never disagree.
225	  CONSTRAINT tasks_completed_at_matches_category CHECK ((status_category = 'completed') = (completed_at IS NOT NULL))
226	);
227	
228	-- Board columns: one project's live tasks, per status, in card order. (rank, id)
229	-- is also the keyset-pagination order, so "next 50 cards in this column" is one
230	-- index range scan; counts per status can be answered from the index alone.
231	CREATE INDEX tasks_board_idx
232	  ON tasks (project_id, status_id, rank, id)
233	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
234	
235	-- "My open tasks / my overdue tasks" across all projects and organizations. Partial:
236	-- only open, live, assigned tasks with a due date — a small slice of the table.
237	-- Queries must repeat this predicate verbatim for the planner to choose the index.
238	-- ("Overdue" itself depends on today's date, which an index predicate cannot
239	-- contain, so the query adds `due_date < <today in the org's zone>`.)
240	CREATE INDEX tasks_open_assigned_due_idx
241	  ON tasks (assignee_id, due_date)
242	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
243	    AND assignee_id IS NOT NULL
244	    AND status_category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled');
245	
246	-- Every task of an assignee, open or not. Also needed by the tasks_assignee_fk
247	-- action: removing a member must find their tasks without scanning the table.
248	CREATE INDEX tasks_assignee_idx ON tasks (assignee_id) WHERE assignee_id IS NOT NULL;
249	
250	
251	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	-- Task triggers
253	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
254	-- BEFORE triggers fire in name order; the numeric infixes make that explicit:
255	--   tasks_10_before_insert   — number + default status (INSERT only)
256	--   tasks_20_sync_status     — status_category + completed_at (INSERT, status change)
257	--   tasks_30_set_updated_at  — updated_at (UPDATE)
258	
259	-- 1) Per-project number + default status.
260	-- SECURITY DEFINER: the counter lives on `projects`, which members may not update.
261	-- The UPDATE … RETURNING is atomic: concurrent inserts into the same project
262	-- queue on that project's row lock for the rest of their transaction, so numbers
263	-- are gap-free and never duplicated (a rolled-back insert does leave a gap).
264	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert() RETURNS trigger
265	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
266	AS $$
267	BEGIN
268	  UPDATE public.projects p
269	     SET task_counter = p.task_counter + 1
270	   WHERE p.id = NEW.project_id
271	     AND p.organization_id = NEW.organization_id
272	     AND p.archived_at IS NULL
273	  RETURNING p.task_counter INTO NEW.number;
274	
275	  IF NEW.number IS NULL THEN
276	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'project % does not exist in organization % or is archived',
277	      NEW.project_id, NEW.organization_id
278	      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
279	  END IF;
280	
281	  IF NEW.status_id IS NULL THEN
282	    -- The project's default status; if none is flagged, its first open column.
283	    SELECT s.id INTO NEW.status_id
284	      FROM public.task_statuses s
285	     WHERE s.project_id = NEW.project_id
286	       AND s.category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled')
287	     ORDER BY s.is_default DESC, s.position, s.id
288	     LIMIT 1;
289	  END IF;
290	
291	  RETURN NEW;
292	END
293	$$;
294	
295	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_10_before_insert
296	  BEFORE INSERT ON tasks
297	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert();
298	
299	-- 2) Keep status_category and completed_at in sync with status_id.
300	-- Runs as the invoking user (no DEFINER needed): it only reads a status the user
301	-- can already see. A status from another project raises here, with a clearer
302	-- message than the composite FK would give.
303	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status() RETURNS trigger
304	LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = ''
305	AS $$
306	DECLARE
307	  v_category public.status_category;
308	BEGIN
309	  SELECT s.category INTO v_category
310	    FROM public.task_statuses s
311	   WHERE s.id = NEW.status_id AND s.project_id = NEW.project_id;
312	
313	  IF v_category IS NULL THEN
314	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'status % does not belong to project %', NEW.status_id, NEW.project_id
315	      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
316	  END IF;
317	
318	  NEW.status_category := v_category;
319	  -- Entering 'completed' stamps completed_at; moving between two completed
320	  -- statuses keeps the original stamp; leaving 'completed' clears it.
321	  NEW.completed_at := CASE
322	    WHEN v_category <> 'completed' THEN NULL
323	    WHEN TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.completed_at IS NOT NULL THEN OLD.completed_at
324	    ELSE pg_catalog.now()
325	  END;
326	  RETURN NEW;
327	END
328	$$;
329	
330	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_20_sync_status
331	  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF status_id ON tasks
332	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status();
333	
334	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_30_set_updated_at
335	  BEFORE UPDATE ON tasks
336	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
337	
338	-- 3) A status whose CATEGORY changes (e.g. an admin turns "QA" from started into
339	-- completed) re-syncs the denormalised copy on all of its tasks — the price of
340	-- the denormalisation, paid on a rare admin action instead of on every read.
341	-- SECURITY DEFINER: app_user has no UPDATE right on these trigger-owned columns.
342	CREATE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category() RETURNS trigger
343	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
344	AS $$
345	BEGIN
346	  IF NEW.category IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.category THEN
347	    UPDATE public.tasks t
348	       SET status_category = NEW.category,
349	           completed_at = CASE WHEN NEW.category = 'completed'
350	                               THEN coalesce(t.completed_at, pg_catalog.now())
351	                               ELSE NULL END
352	     WHERE t.project_id = NEW.project_id   -- (project_id, status_id) = board index
353	       AND t.status_id = NEW.id;
354	  END IF;
355	  RETURN NULL;
356	END
357	$$;
358	
359	CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_propagate_category
360	  AFTER UPDATE OF category ON task_statuses
361	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category();
362	
363	
364	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
365	-- task_labels — many-to-many between tasks and labels
366	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
367	CREATE TABLE task_labels (
368	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL,
369	  task_id          uuid        NOT NULL,
370	  label_id         uuid        NOT NULL,
371	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
372	
373	  PRIMARY KEY (task_id, label_id),  -- "labels of task X"
374	  -- Both sides must be in the same organization as the link row → a task can
375	  -- never carry another tenant's label.
376	  CONSTRAINT task_labels_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
377	    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
378	  CONSTRAINT task_labels_label_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, label_id)
379	    REFERENCES labels (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE
380	);
381	
382	-- "Tasks with label Y" (label filter) + the label-delete cascade.
383	CREATE INDEX task_labels_label_idx ON task_labels (label_id, task_id);

-- =============================================================================
-- 0003_projects_and_tasks.sql — projects, customizable statuses, labels, tasks
-- =============================================================================
-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
--
--   organization ─┬─< project ─┬─< task_status   (each project defines its columns)
--                 │            └─< task >── task_status, assignee (a member)
--                 └─< label >──< task_label >── task
-- =============================================================================


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Enums
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Ordered so that `ORDER BY priority DESC` lists urgent first and none last.
CREATE TYPE task_priority AS ENUM ('none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent');

-- Statuses are custom per project ("QA", "Blocked", "Shipped"…), but the system
-- still needs to know what a status MEANS. Every custom status maps to one fixed
-- category; "open", "overdue", "completed" and cycle-time logic use the category,
-- never status names. (Same approach as Linear's workflow-state types.)
CREATE TYPE status_category AS ENUM ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started', 'completed', 'canceled');


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- projects
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE projects (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Short prefix for human task identifiers: key "WEB" + number 42 → "WEB-42".
  -- Not updatable by the API (0005), so identifiers never change once shared.
  key              text        NOT NULL,
  name             text        NOT NULL,
  description      text,
  -- Last task number handed out in this project; the next task gets +1 (see
  -- app.tasks_before_insert). It exists only to give tasks short, per-project,
  -- human-readable identifiers — WEB-1, WEB-2, … — used in the UI, URLs, commit
  -- messages and conversation ("is WEB-42 done?"). Alternatives rejected:
  --   * max(number) + 1 at insert time — two concurrent inserts read the same
  --     max and collide (unique violation), unless the project is locked anyway;
  --   * one SEQUENCE per project — thousands of schema objects created at
  --     runtime, outside migrations, awkward to copy/restore per tenant;
  --   * a global sequence — unique, but not per project (WEB-48213, and it leaks
  --     platform-wide volume).
  -- An atomic `UPDATE … RETURNING` on this column is O(1) and race-free. Cost:
  -- concurrent task inserts into the SAME project queue on this row's lock until
  -- the inserting transaction commits (different projects never contend).
  task_counter     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  -- Projects are archived, never deleted by the API: their tasks are history.
  archived_at      timestamptz,
  created_by       uuid        DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  -- Redundant with the PK on its own, but required as the TARGET of composite
  -- foreign keys (organization_id, project_id) from child tables — that is what
  -- guarantees a child row's organization_id equals its project's.
  CONSTRAINT projects_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
  -- Also serves "list an organization's projects" (organization_id is leading).
  CONSTRAINT projects_key_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, key),
  CONSTRAINT projects_key_format CHECK (key ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}$'),
  CONSTRAINT projects_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
  CONSTRAINT projects_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 10000),
  CONSTRAINT projects_task_counter_non_negative CHECK (task_counter >= 0)
);

-- Column list: only user-visible edits bump updated_at, not the task counter that
-- every task insert increments.
CREATE TRIGGER projects_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE OF name, description, archived_at ON projects
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- task_statuses — the customizable board columns of ONE project
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE task_statuses (
  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
  name             text            NOT NULL,
  category         status_category NOT NULL,
  color            text            NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
  -- Column order on the board. A project has a handful of statuses, so reordering
  -- simply rewrites the positions in one transaction (no fractional keys needed).
  position         integer         NOT NULL,
  -- The status new tasks get when none is specified.
  is_default       boolean         NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- Target of tasks' composite FK (project_id, status_id): a task can only use
  -- a status of its OWN project.
  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_id_id_unique UNIQUE (project_id, id),
  -- New work must not start out "done": the default must be an open category.
  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_default_is_open CHECK (NOT is_default OR category IN ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started')),
  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_position_non_negative CHECK (position >= 0)
);

-- Status names are unique per project, ignoring case ("Done" vs "done").
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_name_unique ON task_statuses (project_id, lower(name));
-- At most one default per project (a partial unique index: only rows WHERE
-- is_default participate). "At least one" is handled by the fallback in
-- app.tasks_before_insert.
CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_one_default_per_project ON task_statuses (project_id) WHERE is_default;

CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON task_statuses
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();

-- Every new project starts with a usable board. SECURITY DEFINER because members
-- may create projects (if the organization allows) but only admins may manage
-- statuses directly.
CREATE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO public.task_statuses (organization_id, project_id, name, category, color, position, is_default)
  VALUES
    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Backlog',     'backlog',   '#94a3b8', 0, false),
    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Todo',        'unstarted', '#64748b', 1, true),
    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'In Progress', 'started',   '#f59e0b', 2, false),
    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Done',        'completed', '#22c55e', 3, false),
    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Canceled',    'canceled',  '#ef4444', 4, false);
  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER projects_create_default_statuses
  AFTER INSERT ON projects
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- labels — organization-wide tags
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Scoped to the organization, not the project, so one "bug" label can be used and
-- filtered across every project (cross-project reporting).
CREATE TABLE labels (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  name             text        NOT NULL,
  color            text        NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  CONSTRAINT labels_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
  CONSTRAINT labels_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
  CONSTRAINT labels_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50)
);

CREATE UNIQUE INDEX labels_name_unique ON labels (organization_id, lower(name));

CREATE TRIGGER labels_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON labels
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- tasks
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE tasks (
  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
  -- Per-project sequence number, assigned by trigger (never by the client).
  number           integer         NOT NULL,
  title            text            NOT NULL,
  description      text,           -- Markdown
  -- Optional on INSERT: the trigger fills in the project's default status.
  status_id        uuid            NOT NULL,
  -- DENORMALISED copy of task_statuses.category, maintained by triggers (below).
  -- Why: "open"/"overdue" are the hottest filters, and a partial index can only
  -- use columns of its own table — this keeps "my overdue tasks" a single index
  -- range scan instead of a join through task_statuses.
  status_category  status_category NOT NULL,
  priority         task_priority   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
  -- Single assignee (the Linear/Jira model): keeps "tasks per assignee"
  -- unambiguous and ownership clear. A task_assignees join table is the
  -- migration path if multi-assignee is ever needed.
  assignee_id      uuid,
  due_date         date,
  -- Card order within a board column, as a fractional index key ("a0", "a0V",
  -- "a1"…): a card dropped between two others gets a key between theirs, so a
  -- move rewrites ONE row instead of renumbering the column. Keys are generated by
  -- the API. COLLATE "C" = plain byte order, which those keys are designed for;
  -- a linguistic collation (en_US) would order them incorrectly.
  rank             text            COLLATE "C" NOT NULL,
  -- Set while the task is in a 'completed' status (trigger-maintained); feeds
  -- "completed this week" and cycle-time reporting.
  completed_at     timestamptz,
  created_by       uuid            DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  -- Soft delete: deleted tasks keep their comments and history and can be
  -- restored. Hot indexes below exclude them.
  deleted_at       timestamptz,

  -- Tenant consistency: the task's organization IS its project's organization.
  CONSTRAINT tasks_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  -- The status must belong to the task's project. Deleting a status that still
  -- has tasks is refused (move them first). Default NO ACTION, not RESTRICT, so a
  -- cascading project/organization delete can remove tasks and statuses together.
  CONSTRAINT tasks_status_fk FOREIGN KEY (project_id, status_id)
    REFERENCES task_statuses (project_id, id),
  -- The assignee must be a MEMBER of the task's organization. When the membership
  -- ends, only assignee_id is cleared (Postgres 15+ column-list SET NULL) —
  -- organization_id, part of the same key, is of course kept.
  CONSTRAINT tasks_assignee_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, assignee_id)
    REFERENCES organization_members (organization_id, user_id) ON DELETE SET NULL (assignee_id),

  CONSTRAINT tasks_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id), -- composite FK target
  -- Also the index behind identifier lookups ("WEB-42" → project + number).
  CONSTRAINT tasks_number_unique UNIQUE (project_id, number),
  CONSTRAINT tasks_title_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
  CONSTRAINT tasks_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 50000),
  CONSTRAINT tasks_rank_not_empty CHECK (rank <> ''),
  -- The two trigger-maintained columns can never disagree.
  CONSTRAINT tasks_completed_at_matches_category CHECK ((status_category = 'completed') = (completed_at IS NOT NULL))
);

-- Board columns: one project's live tasks, per status, in card order. (rank, id)
-- is also the keyset-pagination order, so "next 50 cards in this column" is one
-- index range scan; counts per status can be answered from the index alone.
CREATE INDEX tasks_board_idx
  ON tasks (project_id, status_id, rank, id)
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;

-- "My open tasks / my overdue tasks" across all projects and organizations. Partial:
-- only open, live, assigned tasks with a due date — a small slice of the table.
-- Queries must repeat this predicate verbatim for the planner to choose the index.
-- ("Overdue" itself depends on today's date, which an index predicate cannot
-- contain, so the query adds `due_date < <today in the org's zone>`.)
CREATE INDEX tasks_open_assigned_due_idx
  ON tasks (assignee_id, due_date)
  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
    AND assignee_id IS NOT NULL
    AND status_category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled');

-- Every task of an assignee, open or not. Also needed by the tasks_assignee_fk
-- action: removing a member must find their tasks without scanning the table.
CREATE INDEX tasks_assignee_idx ON tasks (assignee_id) WHERE assignee_id IS NOT NULL;


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Task triggers
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- BEFORE triggers fire in name order; the numeric infixes make that explicit:
--   tasks_10_before_insert   — number + default status (INSERT only)
--   tasks_20_sync_status     — status_category + completed_at (INSERT, status change)
--   tasks_30_set_updated_at  — updated_at (UPDATE)

-- 1) Per-project number + default status.
-- SECURITY DEFINER: the counter lives on `projects`, which members may not update.
-- The UPDATE … RETURNING is atomic: concurrent inserts into the same project
-- queue on that project's row lock for the rest of their transaction, so numbers
-- are gap-free and never duplicated (a rolled-back insert does leave a gap).
CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  UPDATE public.projects p
     SET task_counter = p.task_counter + 1
   WHERE p.id = NEW.project_id
     AND p.organization_id = NEW.organization_id
     AND p.archived_at IS NULL
  RETURNING p.task_counter INTO NEW.number;

  IF NEW.number IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'project % does not exist in organization % or is archived',
      NEW.project_id, NEW.organization_id
      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
  END IF;

  IF NEW.status_id IS NULL THEN
    -- The project's default status; if none is flagged, its first open column.
    SELECT s.id INTO NEW.status_id
      FROM public.task_statuses s
     WHERE s.project_id = NEW.project_id
       AND s.category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled')
     ORDER BY s.is_default DESC, s.position, s.id
     LIMIT 1;
  END IF;

  RETURN NEW;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER tasks_10_before_insert
  BEFORE INSERT ON tasks
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert();

-- 2) Keep status_category and completed_at in sync with status_id.
-- Runs as the invoking user (no DEFINER needed): it only reads a status the user
-- can already see. A status from another project raises here, with a clearer
-- message than the composite FK would give.
CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = ''
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_category public.status_category;
BEGIN
  SELECT s.category INTO v_category
    FROM public.task_statuses s
   WHERE s.id = NEW.status_id AND s.project_id = NEW.project_id;

  IF v_category IS NULL THEN
    RAISE EXCEPTION 'status % does not belong to project %', NEW.status_id, NEW.project_id
      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
  END IF;

  NEW.status_category := v_category;
  -- Entering 'completed' stamps completed_at; moving between two completed
  -- statuses keeps the original stamp; leaving 'completed' clears it.
  NEW.completed_at := CASE
    WHEN v_category <> 'completed' THEN NULL
    WHEN TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.completed_at IS NOT NULL THEN OLD.completed_at
    ELSE pg_catalog.now()
  END;
  RETURN NEW;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER tasks_20_sync_status
  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF status_id ON tasks
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status();

CREATE TRIGGER tasks_30_set_updated_at
  BEFORE UPDATE ON tasks
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();

-- 3) A status whose CATEGORY changes (e.g. an admin turns "QA" from started into
-- completed) re-syncs the denormalised copy on all of its tasks — the price of
-- the denormalisation, paid on a rare admin action instead of on every read.
-- SECURITY DEFINER: app_user has no UPDATE right on these trigger-owned columns.
CREATE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.category IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.category THEN
    UPDATE public.tasks t
       SET status_category = NEW.category,
           completed_at = CASE WHEN NEW.category = 'completed'
                               THEN coalesce(t.completed_at, pg_catalog.now())
                               ELSE NULL END
     WHERE t.project_id = NEW.project_id   -- (project_id, status_id) = board index
       AND t.status_id = NEW.id;
  END IF;
  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_propagate_category
  AFTER UPDATE OF category ON task_statuses
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- task_labels — many-to-many between tasks and labels
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE task_labels (
  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL,
  task_id          uuid        NOT NULL,
  label_id         uuid        NOT NULL,
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  PRIMARY KEY (task_id, label_id),  -- "labels of task X"
  -- Both sides must be in the same organization as the link row → a task can
  -- never carry another tenant's label.
  CONSTRAINT task_labels_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT task_labels_label_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, label_id)
    REFERENCES labels (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- "Tasks with label Y" (label filter) + the label-delete cascade.
CREATE INDEX task_labels_label_idx ON task_labels (label_id, task_id);

-- =============================================================================
-- 0004_comments_and_activity.sql — task comments and the task activity history
-- =============================================================================
-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
--
-- A task's timeline in the UI is the merge (by time) of two streams:
--   * task_comments   — what people SAID (user-authored, editable, soft-deletable)
--   * task_activities — what CHANGED: who changed which field, from what, to what,
--                       when (system-recorded, append-only, immutable)
-- =============================================================================


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- task_comments
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
CREATE TABLE task_comments (
  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL,
  task_id          uuid        NOT NULL,
  -- Defaults to the requesting user and is not insertable by the API (0005),
  -- so a comment cannot be posted "as" someone else. Kept (as NULL = "former
  -- user") if the user is deleted, so the conversation survives.
  author_id        uuid        DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  body             text        NOT NULL,  -- Markdown
  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
  -- NULL until the body is first edited (trigger-maintained) → "edited" badge.
  edited_at        timestamptz,
  -- Soft delete: the API shows "comment deleted" in place, keeping the thread.
  deleted_at       timestamptz,

  CONSTRAINT task_comments_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT task_comments_body_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(body)) BETWEEN 1 AND 20000)
);

-- A task's comments in order, paginated by (created_at, id). Also serves the
-- task-delete cascade (task_id equality, organization_id checked as a filter).
CREATE INDEX task_comments_task_idx ON task_comments (task_id, created_at, id);

CREATE FUNCTION app.task_comments_mark_edited() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
  IF NEW.body IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.body THEN
    NEW.edited_at := pg_catalog.now();
  END IF;
  RETURN NEW;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER task_comments_mark_edited
  BEFORE UPDATE OF body ON task_comments
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_comments_mark_edited();


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- task_activities — append-only audit trail of task changes
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Design choice: rows are written by TRIGGERS on tasks/task_labels, not by API
-- code. An audit trail is only trustworthy if it is complete, and triggers record
-- every change regardless of which code path (API, script, future service) made
-- it. The actor comes from the same request setting row-level security uses
-- (app.user_id); NULL actor = a system change (migration, seed).
-- Rows are immutable: app_user may only SELECT (0005).
CREATE TYPE task_activity_kind AS ENUM (
  'created',        -- task created
  'updated',        -- one tracked field changed (see `field`)
  'deleted',        -- soft-deleted
  'restored',       -- soft-delete undone
  'label_added',
  'label_removed'
);

CREATE TABLE task_activities (
  id               uuid               PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
  organization_id  uuid               NOT NULL,
  task_id          uuid               NOT NULL,
  actor_id         uuid               REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  kind             task_activity_kind NOT NULL,
  -- For kind = 'updated': which field changed. One row per field, so the
  -- timeline can render "Alice changed priority from Low to High".
  field            text,
  -- Before/after values as JSON so one column fits every field type. Status
  -- and label values are SNAPSHOTS ({"id", "name", …}): history must show the
  -- name a status had at the time, even if it is renamed or deleted later.
  old_value        jsonb,
  new_value        jsonb,
  created_at       timestamptz        NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),

  -- History lives and dies with its task: kept through soft delete; removed only
  -- by a hard delete (i.e. deleting the whole project/organization).
  CONSTRAINT task_activities_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  CONSTRAINT task_activities_field_matches_kind CHECK ((kind = 'updated') = (field IS NOT NULL)),
  CONSTRAINT task_activities_field_known
    CHECK (field IN ('title', 'description', 'status', 'priority', 'assignee', 'due_date'))
);

-- One task's timeline, newest first, keyset-paginated by (created_at, id).
CREATE INDEX task_activities_task_idx ON task_activities (task_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);


-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- Recording task changes
-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
-- SECURITY DEFINER: app_user has no INSERT right on task_activities — only these
-- trigger functions can write history.

-- INSERT → one 'created' row.
CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_creation() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
BEGIN
  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind)
  VALUES (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, app.current_user_id(), 'created');
  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER tasks_record_creation
  AFTER INSERT ON tasks
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_creation();

-- {"id", "name", "category"} of a status at this moment (NULL if it doesn't exist).
CREATE FUNCTION app.status_snapshot(p_status_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
  SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', s.id, 'name', s.name, 'category', s.category)
    FROM public.task_statuses s
   WHERE s.id = p_status_id
$$;

-- UPDATE → one row per changed tracked field, plus deleted/restored transitions.
-- Not tracked: rank (card reordering is noise in a history) and the trigger-owned
-- columns (status_category, completed_at, updated_at), which follow from status.
CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_changes() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_actor uuid := app.current_user_id();
BEGIN
  -- AFTER triggers queued by a cascade fire at the END of the outer statement.
  -- Deleting an organization ends its memberships, whose FK action clears
  -- tasks.assignee_id (an UPDATE → this trigger) — but by the time this trigger
  -- runs, the same cascade has already deleted the task. Nothing to record then;
  -- inserting would violate task_activities' foreign key. (Caught by
  -- api/test/schema.test.ts › "cascading through every table".)
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tasks t WHERE t.id = NEW.id) THEN
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;

  IF (OLD.deleted_at IS NULL) <> (NEW.deleted_at IS NULL) THEN
    INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind)
    VALUES (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, v_actor,
            CASE WHEN NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'deleted' ELSE 'restored' END::public.task_activity_kind);
  END IF;

  -- One statement for all fields: each VALUES row is (field, old, new, changed?).
  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind, field, old_value, new_value)
  SELECT NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, v_actor, 'updated', c.field, c.old_value, c.new_value
    FROM (VALUES
      ('title',       pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.title),    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.title),
                      OLD.title IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.title),
      -- Descriptions can be 50k characters: record THAT it changed, not a copy.
      ('description', NULL::jsonb,                       NULL::jsonb,
                      OLD.description IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.description),
      ('status',      app.status_snapshot(OLD.status_id), app.status_snapshot(NEW.status_id),
                      OLD.status_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status_id),
      ('priority',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.priority), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.priority),
                      OLD.priority IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.priority),
      ('assignee',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.assignee_id), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.assignee_id),
                      OLD.assignee_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.assignee_id),
      ('due_date',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.due_date), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.due_date),
                      OLD.due_date IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.due_date)
    ) AS c(field, old_value, new_value, changed)
   WHERE c.changed;

  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

-- Column list: the trigger does not even fire for rank-only updates (board drags).
CREATE TRIGGER tasks_record_changes
  AFTER UPDATE OF title, description, status_id, priority, assignee_id, due_date, deleted_at ON tasks
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_changes();

-- task_labels INSERT/DELETE → label_added / label_removed.
CREATE FUNCTION app.task_labels_record_change() RETURNS trigger
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
AS $$
DECLARE
  v_link  public.task_labels; -- the link row that was added or removed
  v_label jsonb;
BEGIN
  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN v_link := NEW; ELSE v_link := OLD; END IF;

  -- When the TASK itself is being hard-deleted (organization/project deletion
  -- cascading down), there is no history left to append to — and inserting would
  -- violate task_activities' foreign key. Skip.
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tasks t WHERE t.id = v_link.task_id) THEN
    RETURN NULL;
  END IF;

  -- Snapshot the label; if the LABEL is being deleted (cascade), only its id remains.
  SELECT coalesce(
           (SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', l.id, 'name', l.name, 'color', l.color)
              FROM public.labels l WHERE l.id = v_link.label_id),
           pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', v_link.label_id))
    INTO v_label;

  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind, old_value, new_value)
  VALUES (v_link.organization_id, v_link.task_id, app.current_user_id(),
          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN 'label_added' ELSE 'label_removed' END::public.task_activity_kind,
          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN v_label END,
          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN v_label END);
  RETURN NULL;
END
$$;

CREATE TRIGGER task_labels_record_change
  AFTER INSERT OR DELETE ON task_labels
  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_labels_record_change();
