- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:

schema.name: PowerShell
schema.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.

  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:

    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)

  - When issuing multiple commands:

    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.

  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: SubagentHandback
tools.description:
Deliver your final report to the agent that spawned you (your caller). Use it once, for that hand-off only: when your work is complete, call SubagentHandback({message: <your full report>}). The call ends your run, so do everything else first and put everything your caller needs in that one report. It is not a messaging channel: do not use it for progress updates or questions.

Only a report delivered through SubagentHandback reaches your caller; plain text you write at the end of your run is NOT delivered. There is no recipient parameter: the report can only go to your caller.

1	-- =============================================================================
2	-- 0001_foundation.sql — request role, `app` schema, shared trigger helpers
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1). Frozen once reviewed: fixes ship as new migrations.
5	--
6	-- What: the primitives every later migration builds on; no domain tables here.
7	-- Why:  keeping infrastructure out of the table migrations lets 0002–0004 read
8	--       as pure data modelling, and 0005 as pure access control.
9	--
10	-- Conventions used throughout the schema (explained once, here):
11	--   * Primary keys are `uuid DEFAULT uuidv7()` (built into Postgres 18). v7 UUIDs
12	--     start with a millisecond timestamp, so new rows land at the right-hand edge
13	--     of the B-tree (like a bigserial, no random page splits as with v4), yet they
14	--     are globally unique, safe to expose in URLs (no "you are customer #312"
15	--     leakage) and can be generated by clients for optimistic UI.
16	--   * Every tenant-owned row carries `organization_id`, even when it is derivable
17	--     through a parent. Composite foreign keys (organization_id, parent_id) then
18	--     make a cross-tenant reference impossible, and row-level security (0005) can
19	--     filter every table without joins.
20	--   * Timestamps are `timestamptz` (an instant); due dates are `date` (a calendar
21	--     day with no zone — "due on the 20th" must not shift with the viewer's zone).
22	--   * Lengths and formats are CHECK constraints, so every writer (API, scripts,
23	--     a future service) gets the same validation as the GraphQL layer.
24	-- =============================================================================
25	
26	
27	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	-- Request role: app_user
29	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
30	-- Every API request runs inside one transaction that begins with
31	--     SET LOCAL ROLE app_user;
32	--     SELECT set_config('app.user_id', '<authenticated user uuid>', true);
33	-- app_user owns no tables, so row-level security policies (0005) always apply to
34	-- it. The schema owner (the role running these migrations) bypasses RLS; it is
35	-- used only by migrations, seeds and the SECURITY DEFINER functions below.
36	-- In production the API would log in as a role that is a member of app_user.
37	--
38	-- Roles are cluster-wide objects (shared by every database on the server), so
39	-- this is "create if missing" instead of a plain CREATE ROLE.
40	DO $$
41	BEGIN
42	  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'app_user') THEN
43	    CREATE ROLE app_user NOLOGIN;
44	  END IF;
45	END
46	$$;
47	
48	
49	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
50	-- `app` schema: infrastructure functions (auth helpers, trigger functions)
51	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
52	-- Keeps `public` = data only, which is also exactly what kysely-codegen turns
53	-- into TypeScript types.
54	-- Only roles granted USAGE on it (app_user, in 0005) can reach its functions, and
55	-- 0005 also revokes the default PUBLIC execute right, granting back only what
56	-- app_user needs.
57	CREATE SCHEMA app;
58	
59	
60	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
61	-- app.current_user_id() — who is making this request?
62	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
63	-- Reads the transaction-local setting written at the start of each request.
64	-- `true` = return NULL instead of erroring when the setting was never set.
65	-- `nullif(…, '')`: once a custom setting has been used in a session, Postgres
66	-- reports it as '' (not NULL) after that transaction ends, and ''::uuid would
67	-- throw. Verified in api/test/db.test.ts — this keeps "no user" = NULL, which
68	-- every policy treats as "sees nothing" (fail closed).
69	-- Also used as a column DEFAULT (tasks.created_by, …) so authorship cannot be
70	-- spoofed: app_user is not granted INSERT on those columns (0005).
71	CREATE FUNCTION app.current_user_id() RETURNS uuid
72	LANGUAGE sql STABLE PARALLEL SAFE
73	AS $$
74	  SELECT nullif(pg_catalog.current_setting('app.user_id', true), '')::uuid
75	$$;
76	
77	
78	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
79	-- app.set_updated_at() — keeps `updated_at` honest
80	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
81	-- BEFORE UPDATE trigger body shared by every table with an `updated_at` column.
82	-- Doing it in the database means no code path can forget it. `now()` is the
83	-- transaction start time, so all rows changed in one request share a timestamp.
84	CREATE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at() RETURNS trigger
85	LANGUAGE plpgsql
86	AS $$
87	BEGIN
88	  NEW.updated_at := pg_catalog.now();
89	  RETURN NEW;
90	END
91	$$;

1	-- =============================================================================
2	-- 0002_tenancy.sql — users, organizations (tenants), settings, memberships/roles
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
5	--
6	-- Model: a USER is a global identity (one login, many organizations). An
7	-- ORGANIZATION is the tenant boundary — "organization" and "workspace" are the
8	-- same concept in this product. ORGANIZATION_MEMBERS is the many-to-many link that
9	-- also carries the user's ROLE in that organization (RBAC is per organization).
10	--
11	-- Why many-to-many (a membership table) instead of `users.organization_id`:
12	--   If every user belonged to exactly one organization — typical of a product sold
13	--   to single companies — organization_id and role could simply be columns on
14	--   `users` (one organization → many users), and organization_members would not
15	--   exist. That assumption does not hold for a project-management platform.
16	--   Example: a group that runs several companies — Compliance Foundry, Comperis
17	--   Cybersecurity and Fixpliance AI — is three organizations, each with its own
18	--   projects, members and settings, yet the same people may work in two or all
19	--   three of them. They should use ONE login and switch between organizations,
20	--   not hold three accounts. So one organization has many users AND one user has
21	--   many organizations: many-to-many, which needs a link table.
22	--   The link row is also the only correct home for the ROLE: the same person can
23	--   be an admin in one organization and a viewer in another, which a single
24	--   users.role column cannot express.
25	--   Cost: "what may this user do here?" is a membership lookup rather than a
26	--   column read — one index-only scan (organization_members_user_idx below).
27	-- =============================================================================
28	
29	
30	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
31	-- Roles, in ascending order of power.
32	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
33	-- A Postgres enum (not text + CHECK) because enum values compare by declaration
34	-- order: `role >= 'admin'` means "admin or owner", which is how every permission
35	-- check in 0005 is written. Adding a role later is `ALTER TYPE … ADD VALUE …
36	-- BEFORE/AFTER`, which preserves the ordering.
37	--   viewer — read-only access to everything in the organization
38	--   member — creates and edits tasks, comments, labels
39	--   admin  — manages projects, statuses, settings and non-owner members
40	--   owner  — everything, incl. managing owners and deleting the organization
41	CREATE TYPE organization_role AS ENUM ('viewer', 'member', 'admin', 'owner');
42	
43	
44	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	-- users — global identities
46	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
47	-- Authentication is out of scope (no password/IdP columns); in production this row
48	-- would be keyed to an identity provider subject.
49	CREATE TABLE users (
50	  id            uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
51	  email         text        NOT NULL,
52	  display_name  text        NOT NULL,
53	  avatar_url    text,
54	  created_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
55	  updated_at    timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
56	
57	  CONSTRAINT users_email_unique UNIQUE (email),
58	  -- Stored normalised (trimmed + lower-case), so the plain UNIQUE above is
59	  -- effectively case-insensitive without the citext extension.
60	  CONSTRAINT users_email_normalized CHECK (email = lower(btrim(email)) AND email LIKE '%_@_%'),
61	  CONSTRAINT users_display_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(display_name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
62	  CONSTRAINT users_avatar_url_length CHECK (avatar_url IS NULL OR char_length(avatar_url) <= 2048)
63	);
64	
65	CREATE TRIGGER users_set_updated_at
66	  BEFORE UPDATE ON users
67	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
68	
69	
70	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
71	-- organizations — the tenant
72	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	CREATE TABLE organizations (
74	  id          uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
75	  name        text        NOT NULL,
76	  -- URL identifier: app.example.com/acme/… Lower-case, digits, inner hyphens.
77	  slug        text        NOT NULL,
78	  created_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
79	  updated_at  timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
80	
81	  CONSTRAINT organizations_slug_unique UNIQUE (slug),
82	  CONSTRAINT organizations_slug_format CHECK (slug ~ '^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9-]{0,46}[a-z0-9])?$'),
83	  CONSTRAINT organizations_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100)
84	);
85	
86	CREATE TRIGGER organizations_set_updated_at
87	  BEFORE UPDATE ON organizations
88	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
89	
90	
91	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
92	-- organization_settings — organization-level (workspace-level) settings
93	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
94	-- One row per organization, with TYPED columns rather than a jsonb bag: each
95	-- setting gets a real type, a default and a CHECK, and adding a setting is a
96	-- reviewed migration. (jsonb is the right call only for user-defined/unknown keys.)
97	-- Kept apart from `organizations` because settings are edited by a different
98	-- audience (admins) and change on a different cadence than the tenant identity.
99	CREATE TABLE organization_settings (
100	  organization_id              uuid        PRIMARY KEY REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
101	  -- IANA zone that defines "today" for the organization — and therefore what
102	  -- "overdue" means (a task due on the 20th is overdue from the 21st *there*).
103	  timezone                     text        NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UTC',
104	  -- First day of the week in calendar views: 0 = Sunday … 6 = Saturday (ISO: 1).
105	  week_starts_on               smallint    NOT NULL DEFAULT 1,
106	  -- Lets admins decide whether plain members may create projects; enforced by
107	  -- the projects INSERT policy in 0005 (settings drive authorization).
108	  members_can_create_projects  boolean     NOT NULL DEFAULT true,
109	  updated_at                   timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
110	
111	  -- Evaluating a zone conversion rejects unknown zone names ("Mars/Olympus") with
112	  -- an error, so only real IANA zones are ever stored.
113	  CONSTRAINT organization_settings_timezone_valid CHECK ((now() AT TIME ZONE timezone) IS NOT NULL),
114	  CONSTRAINT organization_settings_week_starts_on_range CHECK (week_starts_on BETWEEN 0 AND 6)
115	);
116	
117	CREATE TRIGGER organization_settings_set_updated_at
118	  BEFORE UPDATE ON organization_settings
119	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
120	
121	-- Every organization always has a settings row (created with the defaults), so
122	-- readers never need a LEFT JOIN + COALESCE. SECURITY DEFINER: the settings row
123	-- is created on behalf of whoever created the organization, whatever their grants.
124	CREATE FUNCTION app.organizations_create_settings() RETURNS trigger
125	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
126	AS $$
127	BEGIN
128	  INSERT INTO public.organization_settings (organization_id) VALUES (NEW.id);
129	  RETURN NULL; -- AFTER trigger: return value ignored
130	END
131	$$;
132	
133	CREATE TRIGGER organizations_create_settings
134	  AFTER INSERT ON organizations
135	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.organizations_create_settings();
136	
137	
138	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
139	-- organization_members — who belongs to which organization, with which role
140	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
141	-- The users ↔ organizations many-to-many link (rationale: header of this file).
142	CREATE TABLE organization_members (
143	  organization_id  uuid              NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
144	  -- Deleting a user removes their memberships (their tasks become unassigned via
145	  -- the ON DELETE SET NULL on tasks — see 0003).
146	  user_id          uuid              NOT NULL REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
147	  role             organization_role NOT NULL DEFAULT 'member',
148	  created_at       timestamptz       NOT NULL DEFAULT now(), -- "joined at"
149	  updated_at       timestamptz       NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
150	
151	  -- PK serves "who is in organization X" (organization_id first) and is the
152	  -- target of tasks' composite assignee FK.
153	  PRIMARY KEY (organization_id, user_id)
154	);
155	
156	-- The reverse direction, "which organizations is user Y in, with what role", runs
157	-- at the start of EVERY request (row-level security). Covering index: the
158	-- membership lookup is answered from the index alone (index-only scan).
159	CREATE INDEX organization_members_user_idx
160	  ON organization_members (user_id, organization_id) INCLUDE (role);
161	
162	CREATE TRIGGER organization_members_set_updated_at
163	  BEFORE UPDATE ON organization_members
164	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
165	
166	
167	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
168	-- Invariant: an organization always has at least one owner
169	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	-- Not expressible as a CHECK (it spans rows), so it is a CONSTRAINT TRIGGER.
171	-- DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED: the check runs at COMMIT, so ownership can be
172	-- transferred in one transaction (promote the new owner, then demote/remove the
173	-- old one) without tripping on the intermediate state.
174	-- Deleting the whole organization is allowed: by commit time the organization row
175	-- is gone, so there is nothing left to protect.
176	CREATE FUNCTION app.organization_keeps_an_owner() RETURNS trigger
177	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
178	AS $$
179	BEGIN
180	  IF OLD.role = 'owner'
181	     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.organizations o WHERE o.id = OLD.organization_id)
182	     AND NOT EXISTS (
183	       SELECT 1 FROM public.organization_members m
184	        WHERE m.organization_id = OLD.organization_id AND m.role = 'owner')
185	  THEN
186	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'organization % must keep at least one owner', OLD.organization_id
187	      USING ERRCODE = 'check_violation',
188	            HINT = 'Promote another member to owner before removing or demoting this one.';
189	  END IF;
190	  RETURN NULL;
191	END
192	$$;
193	
194	CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER organization_members_keep_an_owner
195	  AFTER UPDATE OF role OR DELETE ON organization_members
196	  DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED
197	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.organization_keeps_an_owner();
198

1	-- =============================================================================
2	-- 0003_projects_and_tasks.sql — projects, customizable statuses, labels, tasks
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
5	--
6	--   organization ─┬─< project ─┬─< task_status   (each project defines its columns)
7	--                 │            └─< task >── task_status, assignee (a member)
8	--                 └─< label >──< task_label >── task
9	-- =============================================================================
10	
11	
12	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
13	-- Enums
14	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
15	-- Ordered so that `ORDER BY priority DESC` lists urgent first and none last.
16	CREATE TYPE task_priority AS ENUM ('none', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'urgent');
17	
18	-- Statuses are custom per project ("QA", "Blocked", "Shipped"…), but the system
19	-- still needs to know what a status MEANS. Every custom status maps to one fixed
20	-- category; "open", "overdue", "completed" and cycle-time logic use the category,
21	-- never status names. (Same approach as Linear's workflow-state types.)
22	CREATE TYPE status_category AS ENUM ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started', 'completed', 'canceled');
23	
24	
25	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
26	-- projects
27	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
28	CREATE TABLE projects (
29	  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
30	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
31	  -- Short prefix for human task identifiers: key "WEB" + number 42 → "WEB-42".
32	  -- Not updatable by the API (0005), so identifiers never change once shared.
33	  key              text        NOT NULL,
34	  name             text        NOT NULL,
35	  description      text,
36	  -- Last task number handed out in this project; the next task gets +1 (see
37	  -- app.tasks_before_insert). It exists only to give tasks short, per-project,
38	  -- human-readable identifiers — WEB-1, WEB-2, … — used in the UI, URLs, commit
39	  -- messages and conversation ("is WEB-42 done?"). Alternatives rejected:
40	  --   * max(number) + 1 at insert time — two concurrent inserts read the same
41	  --     max and collide (unique violation), unless the project is locked anyway;
42	  --   * one SEQUENCE per project — thousands of schema objects created at
43	  --     runtime, outside migrations, awkward to copy/restore per tenant;
44	  --   * a global sequence — unique, but not per project (WEB-48213, and it leaks
45	  --     platform-wide volume).
46	  -- An atomic `UPDATE … RETURNING` on this column is O(1) and race-free. Cost:
47	  -- concurrent task inserts into the SAME project queue on this row's lock until
48	  -- the inserting transaction commits (different projects never contend).
49	  task_counter     integer     NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
50	  -- Projects are archived, never deleted by the API: their tasks are history.
51	  archived_at      timestamptz,
52	  created_by       uuid        DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
53	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
54	  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
55	
56	  -- Redundant with the PK on its own, but required as the TARGET of composite
57	  -- foreign keys (organization_id, project_id) from child tables — that is what
58	  -- guarantees a child row's organization_id equals its project's.
59	  CONSTRAINT projects_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
60	  -- Also serves "list an organization's projects" (organization_id is leading).
61	  CONSTRAINT projects_key_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, key),
62	  CONSTRAINT projects_key_format CHECK (key ~ '^[A-Z][A-Z0-9]{1,9}$'),
63	  CONSTRAINT projects_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 100),
64	  CONSTRAINT projects_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 10000),
65	  CONSTRAINT projects_task_counter_non_negative CHECK (task_counter >= 0)
66	);
67	
68	-- Column list: only user-visible edits bump updated_at, not the task counter that
69	-- every task insert increments.
70	CREATE TRIGGER projects_set_updated_at
71	  BEFORE UPDATE OF name, description, archived_at ON projects
72	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
73	
74	
75	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
76	-- task_statuses — the customizable board columns of ONE project
77	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
78	CREATE TABLE task_statuses (
79	  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
80	  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
81	  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
82	  name             text            NOT NULL,
83	  category         status_category NOT NULL,
84	  color            text            NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
85	  -- Column order on the board. A project has a handful of statuses, so reordering
86	  -- simply rewrites the positions in one transaction (no fractional keys needed).
87	  position         integer         NOT NULL,
88	  -- The status new tasks get when none is specified.
89	  is_default       boolean         NOT NULL DEFAULT false,
90	  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
91	  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
92	
93	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
94	    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
95	  -- Target of tasks' composite FK (project_id, status_id): a task can only use
96	  -- a status of its OWN project.
97	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_project_id_id_unique UNIQUE (project_id, id),
98	  -- New work must not start out "done": the default must be an open category.
99	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_default_is_open CHECK (NOT is_default OR category IN ('backlog', 'unstarted', 'started')),
100	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
101	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50),
102	  CONSTRAINT task_statuses_position_non_negative CHECK (position >= 0)
103	);
104	
105	-- Status names are unique per project, ignoring case ("Done" vs "done").
106	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_name_unique ON task_statuses (project_id, lower(name));
107	-- At most one default per project (a partial unique index: only rows WHERE
108	-- is_default participate). "At least one" is handled by the fallback in
109	-- app.tasks_before_insert.
110	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX task_statuses_one_default_per_project ON task_statuses (project_id) WHERE is_default;
111	
112	CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_set_updated_at
113	  BEFORE UPDATE ON task_statuses
114	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
115	
116	-- Every new project starts with a usable board. SECURITY DEFINER because members
117	-- may create projects (if the organization allows) but only admins may manage
118	-- statuses directly.
119	CREATE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses() RETURNS trigger
120	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
121	AS $$
122	BEGIN
123	  INSERT INTO public.task_statuses (organization_id, project_id, name, category, color, position, is_default)
124	  VALUES
125	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Backlog',     'backlog',   '#94a3b8', 0, false),
126	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Todo',        'unstarted', '#64748b', 1, true),
127	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'In Progress', 'started',   '#f59e0b', 2, false),
128	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Done',        'completed', '#22c55e', 3, false),
129	    (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, 'Canceled',    'canceled',  '#ef4444', 4, false);
130	  RETURN NULL;
131	END
132	$$;
133	
134	CREATE TRIGGER projects_create_default_statuses
135	  AFTER INSERT ON projects
136	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.projects_create_default_statuses();
137	
138	
139	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
140	-- labels — organization-wide tags
141	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	-- Scoped to the organization, not the project, so one "bug" label can be used and
143	-- filtered across every project (cross-project reporting).
144	CREATE TABLE labels (
145	  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
146	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL REFERENCES organizations (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
147	  name             text        NOT NULL,
148	  color            text        NOT NULL DEFAULT '#6b7280',
149	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
150	  updated_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
151	
152	  CONSTRAINT labels_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id),
153	  CONSTRAINT labels_color_format CHECK (color ~ '^#[0-9a-f]{6}$'),
154	  CONSTRAINT labels_name_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(name)) BETWEEN 1 AND 50)
155	);
156	
157	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX labels_name_unique ON labels (organization_id, lower(name));
158	
159	CREATE TRIGGER labels_set_updated_at
160	  BEFORE UPDATE ON labels
161	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();
162	
163	
164	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
165	-- tasks
166	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
167	CREATE TABLE tasks (
168	  id               uuid            PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
169	  organization_id  uuid            NOT NULL,
170	  project_id       uuid            NOT NULL,
171	  -- Per-project sequence number, assigned by trigger (never by the client).
172	  number           integer         NOT NULL,
173	  title            text            NOT NULL,
174	  description      text,           -- Markdown
175	  -- Optional on INSERT: the trigger fills in the project's default status.
176	  status_id        uuid            NOT NULL,
177	  -- DENORMALISED copy of task_statuses.category, maintained by triggers (below).
178	  -- Why: "open"/"overdue" are the hottest filters, and a partial index can only
179	  -- use columns of its own table — this keeps "my overdue tasks" a single index
180	  -- range scan instead of a join through task_statuses.
181	  status_category  status_category NOT NULL,
182	  priority         task_priority   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',
183	  -- Single assignee (the Linear/Jira model): keeps "tasks per assignee"
184	  -- unambiguous and ownership clear. A task_assignees join table is the
185	  -- migration path if multi-assignee is ever needed.
186	  assignee_id      uuid,
187	  due_date         date,
188	  -- Card order within a board column, as a fractional index key ("a0", "a0V",
189	  -- "a1"…): a card dropped between two others gets a key between theirs, so a
190	  -- move rewrites ONE row instead of renumbering the column. Keys are generated by
191	  -- the API. COLLATE "C" = plain byte order, which those keys are designed for;
192	  -- a linguistic collation (en_US) would order them incorrectly.
193	  rank             text            COLLATE "C" NOT NULL,
194	  -- Set while the task is in a 'completed' status (trigger-maintained); feeds
195	  -- "completed this week" and cycle-time reporting.
196	  completed_at     timestamptz,
197	  created_by       uuid            DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
198	  created_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
199	  updated_at       timestamptz     NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
200	  -- Soft delete: deleted tasks keep their comments and history and can be
201	  -- restored. Hot indexes below exclude them.
202	  deleted_at       timestamptz,
203	
204	  -- Tenant consistency: the task's organization IS its project's organization.
205	  CONSTRAINT tasks_project_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, project_id)
206	    REFERENCES projects (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
207	  -- The status must belong to the task's project. Deleting a status that still
208	  -- has tasks is refused (move them first). Default NO ACTION, not RESTRICT, so a
209	  -- cascading project/organization delete can remove tasks and statuses together.
210	  CONSTRAINT tasks_status_fk FOREIGN KEY (project_id, status_id)
211	    REFERENCES task_statuses (project_id, id),
212	  -- The assignee must be a MEMBER of the task's organization. When the membership
213	  -- ends, only assignee_id is cleared (Postgres 15+ column-list SET NULL) —
214	  -- organization_id, part of the same key, is of course kept.
215	  CONSTRAINT tasks_assignee_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, assignee_id)
216	    REFERENCES organization_members (organization_id, user_id) ON DELETE SET NULL (assignee_id),
217	
218	  CONSTRAINT tasks_organization_id_id_unique UNIQUE (organization_id, id), -- composite FK target
219	  -- Also the index behind identifier lookups ("WEB-42" → project + number).
220	  CONSTRAINT tasks_number_unique UNIQUE (project_id, number),
221	  CONSTRAINT tasks_title_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(title)) BETWEEN 1 AND 500),
222	  CONSTRAINT tasks_description_length CHECK (description IS NULL OR char_length(description) <= 50000),
223	  CONSTRAINT tasks_rank_not_empty CHECK (rank <> ''),
224	  -- The two trigger-maintained columns can never disagree.
225	  CONSTRAINT tasks_completed_at_matches_category CHECK ((status_category = 'completed') = (completed_at IS NOT NULL))
226	);
227	
228	-- Board columns: one project's live tasks, per status, in card order. (rank, id)
229	-- is also the keyset-pagination order, so "next 50 cards in this column" is one
230	-- index range scan; counts per status can be answered from the index alone.
231	CREATE INDEX tasks_board_idx
232	  ON tasks (project_id, status_id, rank, id)
233	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL;
234	
235	-- "My open tasks / my overdue tasks" across all projects and organizations. Partial:
236	-- only open, live, assigned tasks with a due date — a small slice of the table.
237	-- Queries must repeat this predicate verbatim for the planner to choose the index.
238	-- ("Overdue" itself depends on today's date, which an index predicate cannot
239	-- contain, so the query adds `due_date < <today in the org's zone>`.)
240	CREATE INDEX tasks_open_assigned_due_idx
241	  ON tasks (assignee_id, due_date)
242	  WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
243	    AND assignee_id IS NOT NULL
244	    AND status_category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled');
245	
246	-- Every task of an assignee, open or not. Also needed by the tasks_assignee_fk
247	-- action: removing a member must find their tasks without scanning the table.
248	CREATE INDEX tasks_assignee_idx ON tasks (assignee_id) WHERE assignee_id IS NOT NULL;
249	
250	
251	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
252	-- Task triggers
253	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
254	-- BEFORE triggers fire in name order; the numeric infixes make that explicit:
255	--   tasks_10_before_insert   — number + default status (INSERT only)
256	--   tasks_20_sync_status     — status_category + completed_at (INSERT, status change)
257	--   tasks_30_set_updated_at  — updated_at (UPDATE)
258	
259	-- 1) Per-project number + default status.
260	-- SECURITY DEFINER: the counter lives on `projects`, which members may not update.
261	-- The UPDATE … RETURNING is atomic: concurrent inserts into the same project
262	-- queue on that project's row lock for the rest of their transaction, so numbers
263	-- are gap-free and never duplicated (a rolled-back insert does leave a gap).
264	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert() RETURNS trigger
265	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
266	AS $$
267	BEGIN
268	  UPDATE public.projects p
269	     SET task_counter = p.task_counter + 1
270	   WHERE p.id = NEW.project_id
271	     AND p.organization_id = NEW.organization_id
272	     AND p.archived_at IS NULL
273	  RETURNING p.task_counter INTO NEW.number;
274	
275	  IF NEW.number IS NULL THEN
276	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'project % does not exist in organization % or is archived',
277	      NEW.project_id, NEW.organization_id
278	      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
279	  END IF;
280	
281	  IF NEW.status_id IS NULL THEN
282	    -- The project's default status; if none is flagged, its first open column.
283	    SELECT s.id INTO NEW.status_id
284	      FROM public.task_statuses s
285	     WHERE s.project_id = NEW.project_id
286	       AND s.category NOT IN ('completed', 'canceled')
287	     ORDER BY s.is_default DESC, s.position, s.id
288	     LIMIT 1;
289	  END IF;
290	
291	  RETURN NEW;
292	END
293	$$;
294	
295	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_10_before_insert
296	  BEFORE INSERT ON tasks
297	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_before_insert();
298	
299	-- 2) Keep status_category and completed_at in sync with status_id.
300	-- Runs as the invoking user (no DEFINER needed): it only reads a status the user
301	-- can already see. A status from another project raises here, with a clearer
302	-- message than the composite FK would give.
303	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status() RETURNS trigger
304	LANGUAGE plpgsql SET search_path = ''
305	AS $$
306	DECLARE
307	  v_category public.status_category;
308	BEGIN
309	  SELECT s.category INTO v_category
310	    FROM public.task_statuses s
311	   WHERE s.id = NEW.status_id AND s.project_id = NEW.project_id;
312	
313	  IF v_category IS NULL THEN
314	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'status % does not belong to project %', NEW.status_id, NEW.project_id
315	      USING ERRCODE = 'foreign_key_violation';
316	  END IF;
317	
318	  NEW.status_category := v_category;
319	  -- Entering 'completed' stamps completed_at; moving between two completed
320	  -- statuses keeps the original stamp; leaving 'completed' clears it.
321	  NEW.completed_at := CASE
322	    WHEN v_category <> 'completed' THEN NULL
323	    WHEN TG_OP = 'UPDATE' AND OLD.completed_at IS NOT NULL THEN OLD.completed_at
324	    ELSE pg_catalog.now()
325	  END;
326	  RETURN NEW;
327	END
328	$$;
329	
330	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_20_sync_status
331	  BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF status_id ON tasks
332	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_sync_status();
333	
334	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_30_set_updated_at
335	  BEFORE UPDATE ON tasks
336	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.set_updated_at();

338	-- 3) A status whose CATEGORY changes (e.g. an admin turns "QA" from started into
339	-- completed) re-syncs the denormalised copy on all of its tasks — the price of
340	-- the denormalisation, paid on a rare admin action instead of on every read.
341	-- SECURITY DEFINER: app_user has no UPDATE right on these trigger-owned columns.
342	CREATE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category() RETURNS trigger
343	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
344	AS $$
345	BEGIN
346	  IF NEW.category IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.category THEN
347	    UPDATE public.tasks t
348	       SET status_category = NEW.category,
349	           completed_at = CASE WHEN NEW.category = 'completed'
350	                               THEN coalesce(t.completed_at, pg_catalog.now())
351	                               ELSE NULL END
352	     WHERE t.project_id = NEW.project_id   -- (project_id, status_id) = board index
353	       AND t.status_id = NEW.id;
354	  END IF;
355	  RETURN NULL;
356	END
357	$$;
358	
359	CREATE TRIGGER task_statuses_propagate_category
360	  AFTER UPDATE OF category ON task_statuses
361	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_statuses_propagate_category();

2	-- 0004_comments_and_activity.sql — task comments and the task activity history
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
5	--
6	-- A task's timeline in the UI is the merge (by time) of two streams:
7	--   * task_comments   — what people SAID (user-authored, editable, soft-deletable)
8	--   * task_activities — what CHANGED: who changed which field, from what, to what,
9	--                       when (system-recorded, append-only, immutable)
10	-- =============================================================================
11	
12	
13	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
14	-- task_comments
15	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
16	CREATE TABLE task_comments (
17	  id               uuid        PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
18	  organization_id  uuid        NOT NULL,
19	  task_id          uuid        NOT NULL,
20	  -- Defaults to the requesting user and is not insertable by the API (0005),
21	  -- so a comment cannot be posted "as" someone else. Kept (as NULL = "former
22	  -- user") if the user is deleted, so the conversation survives.
23	  author_id        uuid        DEFAULT app.current_user_id() REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
24	  body             text        NOT NULL,  -- Markdown
25	  created_at       timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
26	  -- NULL until the body is first edited (trigger-maintained) → "edited" badge.
27	  edited_at        timestamptz,
28	  -- Soft delete: the API shows "comment deleted" in place, keeping the thread.
29	  deleted_at       timestamptz,
30	
31	  CONSTRAINT task_comments_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
32	    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
33	  CONSTRAINT task_comments_body_length CHECK (char_length(btrim(body)) BETWEEN 1 AND 20000)
34	);
35	
36	-- A task's comments in order, paginated by (created_at, id). Also serves the
37	-- task-delete cascade (task_id equality, organization_id checked as a filter).
38	CREATE INDEX task_comments_task_idx ON task_comments (task_id, created_at, id);
39	
40	CREATE FUNCTION app.task_comments_mark_edited() RETURNS trigger
41	LANGUAGE plpgsql
42	AS $$
43	BEGIN
44	  IF NEW.body IS DISTINCT FROM OLD.body THEN
45	    NEW.edited_at := pg_catalog.now();
46	  END IF;
47	  RETURN NEW;
48	END
49	$$;

51	CREATE TRIGGER task_comments_mark_edited
52	  BEFORE UPDATE OF body ON task_comments
53	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_comments_mark_edited();

56	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
57	-- task_activities — append-only audit trail of task changes
58	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
59	-- Design choice: rows are written by TRIGGERS on tasks/task_labels, not by API
60	-- code. An audit trail is only trustworthy if it is complete, and triggers record
61	-- every change regardless of which code path (API, script, future service) made
62	-- it. The actor comes from the same request setting row-level security uses
63	-- (app.user_id); NULL actor = a system change (migration, seed).
64	-- Rows are immutable: app_user may only SELECT (0005).
65	CREATE TYPE task_activity_kind AS ENUM (
66	  'created',        -- task created
67	  'updated',        -- one tracked field changed (see `field`)
68	  'deleted',        -- soft-deleted
69	  'restored',       -- soft-delete undone
70	  'label_added',
71	  'label_removed'
72	);
73	
74	CREATE TABLE task_activities (
75	  id               uuid               PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT uuidv7(),
76	  organization_id  uuid               NOT NULL,
77	  task_id          uuid               NOT NULL,
78	  actor_id         uuid               REFERENCES users (id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
79	  kind             task_activity_kind NOT NULL,
80	  -- For kind = 'updated': which field changed. One row per field, so the
81	  -- timeline can render "Alice changed priority from Low to High".
82	  field            text,
83	  -- Before/after values as JSON so one column fits every field type. Status
84	  -- and label values are SNAPSHOTS ({"id", "name", …}): history must show the
85	  -- name a status had at the time, even if it is renamed or deleted later.
86	  old_value        jsonb,
87	  new_value        jsonb,
88	  created_at       timestamptz        NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
89	
90	  -- History lives and dies with its task: kept through soft delete; removed only
91	  -- by a hard delete (i.e. deleting the whole project/organization).
92	  CONSTRAINT task_activities_task_fk FOREIGN KEY (organization_id, task_id)
93	    REFERENCES tasks (organization_id, id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
94	  CONSTRAINT task_activities_field_matches_kind CHECK ((kind = 'updated') = (field IS NOT NULL)),
95	  CONSTRAINT task_activities_field_known
96	    CHECK (field IN ('title', 'description', 'status', 'priority', 'assignee', 'due_date'))
97	);
98	
99	-- One task's timeline, newest first, keyset-paginated by (created_at, id).
100	CREATE INDEX task_activities_task_idx ON task_activities (task_id, created_at DESC, id DESC);
101	
102	
103	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
104	-- Recording task changes
105	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
106	-- SECURITY DEFINER: app_user has no INSERT right on task_activities — only these
107	-- trigger functions can write history.
108	
109	-- INSERT → one 'created' row.
110	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_creation() RETURNS trigger
111	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
112	AS $$
113	BEGIN
114	  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind)
115	  VALUES (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, app.current_user_id(), 'created');
116	  RETURN NULL;
117	END
118	$$;
119	
120	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_record_creation
121	  AFTER INSERT ON tasks
122	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_creation();
123	
124	-- {"id", "name", "category"} of a status at this moment (NULL if it doesn't exist).
125	CREATE FUNCTION app.status_snapshot(p_status_id uuid) RETURNS jsonb
126	LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
127	AS $$
128	  SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', s.id, 'name', s.name, 'category', s.category)
129	    FROM public.task_statuses s
130	   WHERE s.id = p_status_id
131	$$;
132	
133	-- UPDATE → one row per changed tracked field, plus deleted/restored transitions.
134	-- Not tracked: rank (card reordering is noise in a history) and the trigger-owned
135	-- columns (status_category, completed_at, updated_at), which follow from status.
136	CREATE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_changes() RETURNS trigger
137	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
138	AS $$
139	DECLARE
140	  v_actor uuid := app.current_user_id();
141	BEGIN
142	  -- AFTER triggers queued by a cascade fire at the END of the outer statement.
143	  -- Deleting an organization ends its memberships, whose FK action clears
144	  -- tasks.assignee_id (an UPDATE → this trigger) — but by the time this trigger
145	  -- runs, the same cascade has already deleted the task. Nothing to record then;
146	  -- inserting would violate task_activities' foreign key. (Caught by
147	  -- api/test/schema.test.ts › "cascading through every table".)
148	  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tasks t WHERE t.id = NEW.id) THEN
149	    RETURN NULL;
150	  END IF;
151	
152	  IF (OLD.deleted_at IS NULL) <> (NEW.deleted_at IS NULL) THEN
153	    INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind)
154	    VALUES (NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, v_actor,
155	            CASE WHEN NEW.deleted_at IS NOT NULL THEN 'deleted' ELSE 'restored' END::public.task_activity_kind);
156	  END IF;
157	
158	  -- One statement for all fields: each VALUES row is (field, old, new, changed?).
159	  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind, field, old_value, new_value)
160	  SELECT NEW.organization_id, NEW.id, v_actor, 'updated', c.field, c.old_value, c.new_value
161	    FROM (VALUES
162	      ('title',       pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.title),    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.title),
163	                      OLD.title IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.title),
164	      -- Descriptions can be 50k characters: record THAT it changed, not a copy.
165	      ('description', NULL::jsonb,                       NULL::jsonb,
166	                      OLD.description IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.description),
167	      ('status',      app.status_snapshot(OLD.status_id), app.status_snapshot(NEW.status_id),
168	                      OLD.status_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.status_id),
169	      ('priority',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.priority), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.priority),
170	                      OLD.priority IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.priority),
171	      ('assignee',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.assignee_id), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.assignee_id),
172	                      OLD.assignee_id IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.assignee_id),
173	      ('due_date',    pg_catalog.to_jsonb(OLD.due_date), pg_catalog.to_jsonb(NEW.due_date),
174	                      OLD.due_date IS DISTINCT FROM NEW.due_date)
175	    ) AS c(field, old_value, new_value, changed)
176	   WHERE c.changed;
177	
178	  RETURN NULL;
179	END
180	$$;
181	
182	-- Column list: the trigger does not even fire for rank-only updates (board drags).
183	CREATE TRIGGER tasks_record_changes
184	  AFTER UPDATE OF title, description, status_id, priority, assignee_id, due_date, deleted_at ON tasks
185	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.tasks_record_changes();
186	
187	-- task_labels INSERT/DELETE → label_added / label_removed.
188	CREATE FUNCTION app.task_labels_record_change() RETURNS trigger
189	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
190	AS $$
191	DECLARE
192	  v_link  public.task_labels; -- the link row that was added or removed
193	  v_label jsonb;
194	BEGIN
195	  IF TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN v_link := NEW; ELSE v_link := OLD; END IF;
196	
197	  -- When the TASK itself is being hard-deleted (organization/project deletion
198	  -- cascading down), there is no history left to append to — and inserting would
199	  -- violate task_activities' foreign key. Skip.
200	  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.tasks t WHERE t.id = v_link.task_id) THEN
201	    RETURN NULL;
202	  END IF;
203	
204	  -- Snapshot the label; if the LABEL is being deleted (cascade), only its id remains.
205	  SELECT coalesce(
206	           (SELECT pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', l.id, 'name', l.name, 'color', l.color)
207	              FROM public.labels l WHERE l.id = v_link.label_id),
208	           pg_catalog.jsonb_build_object('id', v_link.label_id))
209	    INTO v_label;
210	
211	  INSERT INTO public.task_activities (organization_id, task_id, actor_id, kind, old_value, new_value)
212	  VALUES (v_link.organization_id, v_link.task_id, app.current_user_id(),
213	          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN 'label_added' ELSE 'label_removed' END::public.task_activity_kind,
214	          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'DELETE' THEN v_label END,
215	          CASE WHEN TG_OP = 'INSERT' THEN v_label END);
216	  RETURN NULL;
217	END
218	$$;
219	
220	CREATE TRIGGER task_labels_record_change
221	  AFTER INSERT OR DELETE ON task_labels
222	  FOR EACH ROW EXECUTE FUNCTION app.task_labels_record_change();

1	-- =============================================================================
2	-- 0005_access_control.sql — privileges + row-level security (RLS)
3	-- =============================================================================
4	-- Schema v1 (Task 1.1).
5	--
6	-- Two layers, defence in depth:
7	--   1. The API checks permissions explicitly in its resolvers (readable, unit-tested,
8	--      good error messages).
9	--   2. THIS migration makes the database enforce the same rules for the app_user
10	--      role, so a forgotten check or a buggy query cannot read or write another
11	--      tenant's data, or exceed the caller's role.
12	--
13	-- How a policy knows the caller: each request transaction runs
14	--     SET LOCAL ROLE app_user;
15	--     SELECT set_config('app.user_id', '<uuid>', true);
16	-- and policies call app.current_user_id() / app.user_organization_ids().
17	--
18	-- Two mechanisms, two jobs:
19	--   * GRANTs (incl. COLUMN-level) decide WHICH columns app_user may write at all.
20	--     Immutable columns (ids, organization_id, project_id, task number, authorship,
21	--     trigger-maintained fields) are simply never granted, so even a buggy UPDATE
22	--     cannot move a task to another tenant or rewrite who created it.
23	--   * POLICIES decide WHICH ROWS: tenant membership for reads, role thresholds for
24	--     writes.
25	--
26	-- Permission matrix (minimum organization role):
27	--                         read     create         update             delete
28	--   organization          viewer   (any user)¹    admin              owner
29	--   settings              viewer   (automatic)    admin              —
30	--   members               viewer   admin²         admin²             admin² / self (leave)
31	--   projects              viewer   admin|member³  admin (incl. archive)  — (archive)
32	--   statuses              viewer   admin          admin              admin
33	--   labels                viewer   member         member             admin
34	--   tasks                 viewer   member         member (incl. soft delete) — (soft)
35	--   task labels           viewer   member         —                  member
36	--   comments              viewer   member         author|admin       author|admin (soft)
37	--   activity history      viewer   (triggers)     never              never
38	--   ¹ via app.create_organization(), which also makes the caller the owner
39	--   ² only owners may create, change or remove OWNER memberships
40	--   ³ members only if organization_settings.members_can_create_projects
41	--
42	-- Note on UPDATE semantics: a row the caller may see but not update is silently
43	-- skipped (0 rows affected) rather than raising — the API turns "0 rows" into a
44	-- FORBIDDEN/NOT_FOUND error. INSERTs that fail a policy raise an error.
45	-- =============================================================================
46	
47	
48	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
49	-- Authorization helpers
50	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
51	-- SECURITY DEFINER: they read organization_members WITHOUT going through its RLS
52	-- policy (which itself calls them) — otherwise policies would recurse.
53	-- STABLE: same answer for the whole statement.
54	--
55	-- Performance pattern used in every policy: `(SELECT app.fn())` instead of
56	-- `app.fn()`. The sub-select becomes an InitPlan, evaluated ONCE per query instead
57	-- of once per row, and `organization_id = ANY (<array>)` can use an index.
58	-- The `::uuid[]` cast in `= ANY ((SELECT …)::uuid[])` is load-bearing: without it
59	-- Postgres parses `= ANY ((SELECT …))` as the "ANY (subquery)" form and compares
60	-- the uuid against each ROW of the sub-select (uuid = uuid[] → error).
61	
62	-- Every organization the caller belongs to (empty array when not signed in).
63	CREATE FUNCTION app.user_organization_ids() RETURNS uuid[]
64	LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
65	AS $$
66	  SELECT coalesce(pg_catalog.array_agg(m.organization_id), '{}')
67	    FROM public.organization_members m
68	   WHERE m.user_id = app.current_user_id()
69	$$;
70	
71	-- Does the caller hold at least `p_minimum_role` in this organization?
72	-- Enum order makes this one comparison: owner >= admin >= member >= viewer.
73	CREATE FUNCTION app.has_organization_role(p_organization_id uuid, p_minimum_role public.organization_role)
74	RETURNS boolean
75	LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
76	AS $$
77	  SELECT EXISTS (
78	    SELECT 1
79	      FROM public.organization_members m
80	     WHERE m.organization_id = p_organization_id
81	       AND m.user_id = app.current_user_id()
82	       AND m.role >= p_minimum_role
83	  )
84	$$;
85	
86	-- May the caller create/change/remove a membership that has role `p_role`?
87	-- Admins manage everyone except owners; only owners manage owners.
88	CREATE FUNCTION app.can_manage_member(p_organization_id uuid, p_role public.organization_role)
89	RETURNS boolean
90	LANGUAGE sql STABLE SET search_path = ''
91	AS $$
92	  SELECT app.has_organization_role(p_organization_id, 'admin')
93	     AND (p_role <> 'owner' OR app.has_organization_role(p_organization_id, 'owner'))
94	$$;
95	
96	-- Creating an organization is a chicken-and-egg problem for RLS (you are not yet a
97	-- member of the organization you are creating), so it is one privileged,
98	-- audited entry point: create the organization (+ settings, by trigger) and make
99	-- the caller its owner, atomically.
100	CREATE FUNCTION app.create_organization(p_name text, p_slug text) RETURNS uuid
101	LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = ''
102	AS $$
103	DECLARE
104	  v_user_id         uuid := app.current_user_id();
105	  v_organization_id uuid;
106	BEGIN
107	  IF v_user_id IS NULL THEN
108	    RAISE EXCEPTION 'authentication required' USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege';
109	  END IF;
110	
111	  INSERT INTO public.organizations (name, slug)
112	  VALUES (p_name, p_slug)
113	  RETURNING id INTO v_organization_id;
114	
115	  INSERT INTO public.organization_members (organization_id, user_id, role)
116	  VALUES (v_organization_id, v_user_id, 'owner');
117	
118	  RETURN v_organization_id;
119	END
120	$$;
121	
122	
123	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
124	-- Function & schema privileges
125	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
126	-- New functions are executable by PUBLIC by default. Revoke that for the whole
127	-- `app` schema, then grant back only what app_user calls directly (in policies,
128	-- column defaults and the API). Trigger functions need no grant: privileges on
129	-- them are checked when the trigger is created, not each time it fires.
130	REVOKE ALL ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA app FROM PUBLIC;
131	GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA app, public TO app_user;
132	GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION
133	  app.current_user_id(),
134	  app.user_organization_ids(),
135	  app.has_organization_role(uuid, public.organization_role),
136	  app.can_manage_member(uuid, public.organization_role),
137	  app.create_organization(text, text)
138	TO app_user;
139	
140	
141	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
142	-- users
143	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
144	-- Visible: yourself, and anyone who shares an organization with you (to show
145	-- assignees, authors, member lists). Editable: your own profile only.
146	ALTER TABLE users ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
147	GRANT SELECT ON users TO app_user;
148	GRANT UPDATE (display_name, avatar_url) ON users TO app_user;
149	
150	CREATE POLICY users_select ON users FOR SELECT TO app_user
151	  USING (
152	    id = (SELECT app.current_user_id())
153	    OR EXISTS (
154	      SELECT 1 FROM organization_members m
155	       WHERE m.user_id = users.id
156	         AND m.organization_id = ANY ((SELECT app.user_organization_ids())::uuid[])
157	    )
158	  );
159	
160	CREATE POLICY users_update_self ON users FOR UPDATE TO app_user
161	  USING (id = (SELECT app.current_user_id()))
162	  WITH CHECK (id = (SELECT app.current_user_id()));
163	
164	
165	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
166	-- organizations  (created only through app.create_organization)
167	-- -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
168	ALTER TABLE organizations ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY;
169	GRANT SELECT, DELETE ON organizations TO app_user;
170	GRANT UPDATE (name, slug) ON organizations TO app_user;

1	# =============================================================================
2	# Task Board platform — GraphQL API design (schema v1, Task 1.1)
3	# =============================================================================
4	# What: the complete public API contract for the multi-tenant project-management
5	#       platform. Part 2 implements the Task Board slice of it
6	#       (api/src/graphql/schema.graphql), field-for-field compatible with this file.
7	# Data model behind it: api/db/migrations/0001–0005 (PostgreSQL 18).
8	#
9	# Conventions
10	#   * IDs are the database's UUIDv7 primary keys, exposed as opaque `ID`s.
11	#   * Lists that can grow without bound are cursor-paginated connections
12	#     (`first` / `after`, Relay style). Small bounded lists — a project's statuses,
13	#     a task's labels — are plain lists.
14	#   * Every mutation takes one `input` object and returns a payload object, so
15	#     either side can gain fields later without breaking clients.
16	#   * Errors use the standard GraphQL `errors` array with `extensions.code`:
17	#     UNAUTHENTICATED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, BAD_USER_INPUT, CONFLICT.
18	#     Anything the caller may not see is reported as NOT_FOUND — the API never
19	#     confirms that another tenant's IDs exist.
20	#   * Enum values are UPPER_CASE here and lower_case in Postgres; the API maps them.
21	# =============================================================================
22	
23	"""
24	Documents the minimum organization role needed to use a field, evaluated against
25	the organization that owns the object. Enforced twice: in the resolver (clear
26	error messages) and by row-level security in Postgres (defence in depth).
27	Fields without it require VIEWER, i.e. any membership.
28	"""
29	directive @requiresRole(role: OrganizationRole!) on FIELD_DEFINITION
30	
31	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
32	# Scalars
33	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	
35	"An instant in time: ISO-8601 with offset, e.g. `2026-11-16T09:30:00Z`."
36	scalar DateTime
37	
38	"""
39	A calendar date with no time or zone: `YYYY-MM-DD`. Used for due dates — "due on
40	the 20th" must not shift when viewed from another time zone.
41	"""
42	scalar Date
43	
44	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
45	# Enums
46	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
47	
48	"A member's role within one organization, in ascending order of power."
49	enum OrganizationRole {
50	  "Read-only access to everything in the organization."
51	  VIEWER
52	  "Creates and edits tasks, comments and labels."
53	  MEMBER
54	  "Also manages projects, statuses, settings and non-owner members."
55	  ADMIN
56	  "Full control, including owners and deleting the organization."
57	  OWNER
58	}
59	
60	"Task priority, lowest to highest."
61	enum TaskPriority {
62	  NONE
63	  LOW
64	  MEDIUM
65	  HIGH
66	  URGENT
67	}
68	
69	"""
70	What a (custom) status means. Projects name their statuses freely ("QA",
71	"Blocked"…); each maps to one category, which drives open/overdue/completed logic.
72	"""
73	enum StatusCategory {
74	  BACKLOG
75	  UNSTARTED
76	  STARTED
77	  COMPLETED
78	  CANCELED
79	}
80	
81	enum SortDirection {
82	  ASC
83	  DESC
84	}
85	
86	enum TaskSortField {
87	  "Manual board order. Only meaningful within one status column."
88	  RANK
89	  PRIORITY
90	  DUE_DATE
91	  CREATED_AT
92	  UPDATED_AT
93	  "The per-project sequence number (WEB-1, WEB-2, …)."
94	  NUMBER
95	}
96	
97	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	# Pagination
99	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	
101	"Cursor pagination state. Cursors are opaque; pass `endCursor` as `after`."
102	type PageInfo {
103	  hasNextPage: Boolean!
104	  endCursor: String
105	}

107	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
108	# Identity & tenancy
109	# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
